experiment: E11 graph rebuild after a commit on a deep history
decision: a graph rebuild after one new commit on a 30,000-commit repository fell from a 95.0 to 104.5 ms median per run to 7.4 to 7.5 ms, by remembering what earlier captures read (d6087c97, ownership and graft fixes in 9e6ec1b9); the first capture of a session is unchanged at about 112 to 136 ms
scope: backend capture only, timed in-process around trunk_git::graph capture; not the app's commit-to-usable time, not the frontend, not cold disk cache; one machine, three alternating runs per build of 21 rebuilds each
comparativeVerdict: after faster in every run, ranges disjoint (before min 94.2 ms, after max 8.8 ms)
machine: Apple M5 Pro, 48 GB, macOS, release profile, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 for the build only

before.call: trunk_git::graph::capture on a fresh Repository::open per rebuild, as every app command did

after.call: trunk_git::graph::capture_remembering on a fresh Repository::open per rebuild, with one CommitMemo held across rebuilds, as OpenRepo holds it

fixture.build: git init <dir>; python3 generator.py 30000 | git -C <dir> fast-import --quiet
fixture.shape: seeded (7) random history: about 4% merges of feature into main, feature and topic branches, about 30% of commits in the same second as the one before
fixture.storage: one pack written by fast-import, no commit-graph file
fixture.fresh copy: the generated repository was copied before every run, since each run adds 21 commits

procedure: per run: copy the fixture, time one capture (firstCaptureMs), then 21 times: commit one commit on main with git2 through a separate handle, open a fresh handle and time one capture (rebuildsMs). Runs alternate before, after, three times.
generator:
import sys, random
random.seed(7)
n = int(sys.argv[1])
out = sys.stdout.buffer
t = 1_600_000_000
marks = {}
mark = 0
heads = {"main": None, "feature": None, "topic": None}
def commit(branch, parents, ts):
    global mark
    mark += 1
    msg = f"commit {mark} on {branch}\n".encode()
    out.write(f"commit refs/heads/{branch}\nmark :{mark}\n".encode())
    out.write(f"author A <a@x> {ts} +0000\ncommitter A <a@x> {ts} +0000\n".encode())
    out.write(f"data {len(msg)}\n".encode() + msg)
    if parents:
        out.write(f"from :{parents[0]}\n".encode())
        for p in parents[1:]:
            out.write(f"merge :{p}\n".encode())
    out.write(f"M 644 inline f{mark % 50}.txt\ndata 2\n{mark % 10}\n".encode())
    out.write(b"\n")
    return mark
for i in range(n):
    # same-second runs, like scripted or rebased commits
    if random.random() < 0.7: t += random.randint(1, 600)
    r = random.random()
    if heads["main"] and r < 0.04 and heads["feature"]:
        m = commit("main", [heads["main"], heads["feature"]], t); heads["main"] = m
    elif r < 0.25 and heads["main"]:
        b = "feature" if r < 0.15 else "topic"
        base = heads[b] or heads["main"]
        heads[b] = commit(b, [base], t)
    else:
        heads["main"] = commit("main", [heads["main"]] if heads["main"] else [], t)

probe.placement: src-tauri/git/examples/t440_rebuild.rs in each exported tree, built with cargo build --release -p trunk-git --example t440_rebuild in separate target directories (a shared one reused the first binary)

limitations: the app's end-to-end commit flow also runs the commit, status, the watcher refresh and the frontend; those are not in this number
the probe never moves HEAD, deletes refs or stashes; recapture equality for those moves is held by the graph.rs unit tests, not timed
memory held by the memo was not measured
